properties.title: G-Transformer: Counterfactual Outcome Prediction under Dynamic and Time-varying Treatment Regimes

membership.reason: G-Transformer is a Transformer-based sequential g-computation world model simulating Monte Carlo counterfactual trajectories under dynamic time-varying treatment regimes.
membership.counting_boundary: Verified L3 counterfactual/branching dynamic-treatment-regime world model (WT_EHR, BP_COMPARE).

properties.backbone: Dual Categorical + Continuous Transformer encoders for sequential g-computation

properties.flow: Observed history + dynamic treatment regime g_c -> G-Transformer Monte Carlo rollouts -> counterfactual outcome distributions

properties.purpose: Counterfactual outcome prediction under static and dynamic time-varying treatment regimes.
properties.environment: Tumor growth simulator, CVSim, and MIMIC-IV sepsis cohort

assertions.rationale: Separate Categorical and Continuous Transformer encoders.
Transformer hidden representations h_ca, h_co over covariate-treatment history.
Conditioned on full covariate and treatment history (L_{t-1}, A_{t-1}).

Evaluated matched alternative-action counterfactual predictions from the same initial histories across 4 cancer growth regimes (horizons t=1..4, Table 1; best overall RMSE in 3 of 4 regimes, behind CT on Chemo), 2 CVSim dynamic regimes gc1 vs gc2 (32-step horizon from hour 34, Table 2 & Fig. 2), and illustrative conservative (5L cap) vs liberal fluid regimes in MIMIC-IV sepsis (24h horizon, Fig. 5; no counterfactual ground truth in MIMIC-IV).

Simulates future covariates and outcomes conditioned on static and dynamic counterfactual treatment regimes g_c; quantitatively evaluated against ground truth on Cancer Growth (4 regimes, Table 1) and CVSim (gc1, gc2, Table 2).
Monte Carlo sampling with empirical simulation noise epsilon.

Evaluated one-step (t=1) and multi-step (t=2..4) counterfactual tumor-volume rollouts in Cancer Growth (Table 1), 32-step covariate rollouts in CVSim (Table 2), and 24-hour observational rollouts in MIMIC-IV (Tables 3-4).
Clinical counterfactual prediction under competing dynamic treatment strategies.
Outperforms rMSN, CRN, G-Net, and Causal Transformer on simulated tumor growth and CVSim counterfactual benchmarks.
Evaluated on real-world MIMIC-IV sepsis fluid administration cohort.

evidence_fragments.content: We evaluate G-Transformer extensively using two simulated longitudinal datasets from mechanistic models, and a real-world sepsis ICU dataset from MIMIC-IV. G-Transformer outperforms both classical and state-of-the-art counterfactual prediction models in these settings.

[paraphrase (visual p.6)] Figure 1 shows the G-Transformer architecture with separate Categorical and Continuous Transformer encoders producing hidden states h_ca and h_co, trained with teacher forcing (cross-entropy and MSE losses) and rolled out in the simulation process under counterfactual treatment strategy g_c with categorical sampling and empirical noise.

locator.section_or_table: Section 4.1 Cancer Growth Experiments and Results

evidence_fragments.content: Briefly, we generated four test sets in which four counterfactual regimes were followed for the final four time points in the test set: (1) give only radiotherapy, (2) only chemotherapy, (3) both chemotherapy and radiotherapy, and (4) no treatment.

Table 2 presents a comparison of individual-level and population-level RMSE among linear implementation of g-computation, G-Net, Causal Transformer, and G-Transformer under gc1 and gc2. The G-Transformer outperforms linear implementation of g-computation and G-Net, and considerably outperforms Causal Transformer in this counterfactual prediction task.

We used G-Transformer to simulate covariate trajectories for patients in the test dataset under one conservative fluids strategies (with 5L fluid cap) and a fluid liberal strategy (with no cap). Selected covariates are presented in Figure 5, allowing for comparison of the two counterfactual regimes.

capability_assessments.rationale: Transformer-based sequential g-computation world model with implemented persistent history state, temporal transition dynamics, and learned conditional covariate factorization; evaluated on matched alternative-action counterfactual regime comparisons in Cancer Growth (4 regimes, horizons 1-4), CVSim (dynamic regimes gc1 vs gc2, 32-step horizon), and illustrative fluid regimes in MIMIC-IV (L3).

readiness_assessments.legacy_highest_label: R1 In silico simulators + single-center MIMIC-IV

limitations: Single-center MIMIC-IV cohort + in silico simulators; relies on sequential exchangeability and positivity assumptions.

No ground-truth counterfactual observations exist in MIMIC-IV (Fig. 5 is illustrative with potential censoring/survivor bias from death/discharge); Monte Carlo predictive density does not quantify model parameter uncertainty (pp. 14, 18).

legacy_cells.B: G-Transformer: Counterfactual Outcome Prediction under Dynamic and Time-varying Treatment Regimes
legacy_cells.S: Given a patient’s observed history, what covariate and outcome trajectories are predicted under alternative dynamic treatment strategies?
legacy_cells.T: 8,934 ICU patients identified as septic under Sepsis-3; patients with missing pre-ICU fluid records or ICU admission following cardiac, vascular, or trauma surgery were excluded.
legacy_cells.V: Estimate patient outcomes under clinician-specified treatment strategies to inform treatment decisions.
legacy_cells.AI: Longitudinal EHR covariates: categorical and continuous clinical variables, including demographics, comorbidities, laboratory values, vital signs, urine output, and treatment variables
legacy_cells.AJ: Transformer encoders; separate encoders for categorical and continuous covariates, and a separate Transformer encoder for each MIMIC covariate
legacy_cells.BD: MIMIC sepsis strategies: 1000 mL fluid bolus when blood pressure was below 65 mmHg; total-fluid cap of 5 L or no cap; stop at cap or fluid overload. Simulated CVSim strategies included fluid and vasopressor administration.
legacy_cells.BL: MIMIC evaluation forecast horizon: 24 hours; CVSim trajectories: 66 time steps, with 32 remaining hours predicted after 34 observed hours.
legacy_cells.BS: Monte Carlo sampled future covariate and outcome trajectories under specified treatment strategies
legacy_cells.BV: Cross-entropy loss for categorical variables and mean squared error (MSE) loss for continuous variables
legacy_cells.CR: Empirical interval coverage calibration over time using 5th–95th percentile Monte Carlo intervals, under CVSim gc1 and gc2
legacy_cells.CV: Consistency; sequential exchangeability (no unobserved confounding; all treatment-decision drivers prognostic for outcome are included); positivity (the strategy has non-zero probability of implementation).
legacy_cells.CX: Counterfactual ground truth was available for simulated tumor-growth and CVSim data; MIMIC-IV had no ground-truth counterfactual observations.
legacy_cells.FN: G-Transformer was evaluated on cancer-growth and CVSim simulations with known counterfactuals and on retrospective MIMIC-IV sepsis. It outperformed reported comparison models in the simulations; real-cohort alternative fluid-regime forecasts do not establish prospective treatment benefit.
